question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2x-10y &=10 \\ -x-5y &=5 \\ 2x+10y &=-10.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & -10 & 10 \\ -1 & -5 & 5 \\ 2 & 10 & -10\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & -10 & 10 \\ -1 & -5 & 5 \\ 2 & 10 & -10\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 5 & -5 \\ -1 & -5 & 5 \\ 2 & 10 & -10\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 5 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 10 & -10\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 5 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+5y &=-5.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$, and we have one free variable, $y$. That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-5y-5 \\ y &=y,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-5y-5 \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
